ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ of rectangle $ABCD$ intersect at point $O$. A line passing through point $O$ intersects $AD$ and $BC$ at points $E$ and $F$, respectively. Given $AB=2$ and $BC=3$, what is the area of the shaded region in the figure?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since the diagonals AC and BD of rectangle ABCD intersect at point O, \\
it follows that the area of the blank triangle within quadrilateral ABFE is equal to the area of the shaded triangle within quadrilateral EDCF.\\
Therefore, finding the area of the shaded part can be considered as finding the area of quadrilateral ABFE.\\
Hence, the area of the shaded part is: $\frac{2\times 3}{2}=\boxed{3}$.

method.method_draft: Use central symmetry and area pairing. From the figure, the shaded regions are AEO, BOF, and DCO; the unshaded complementary regions are ABO, DEO, and CFO. Since O is the intersection of the diagonals of a rectangle, O is the center of 180-degree rotational symmetry. Under this half-turn, triangle DCO maps to triangle ABO, so they have equal area. Also, because EF passes through O, E and F are paired by the same central symmetry; hence triangle AEO maps to triangle CFO, and triangle BOF maps to triangle DEO. Therefore the total shaded area equals the total unshaded area. The whole rectangle has area AB·BC=2·3=6, so the shaded half is 3.
